conditions: f defined on an open interval containing x; finite two-sided limit exists.
spoken_aliases: f prime of x equals the limit as h approaches zero of the fraction with numerator f of open parenthesis x plus h close parenthesis minus f of x and denominator h
the derivative of f at x equals the limit as h tends to zero of open parenthesis f of the quantity x plus h minus f of x close parenthesis all divided by h

evidence: This is the definition of a finite ordinary two-sided derivative: the limit of the slopes between (x,f(x)) and (x+h,f(x+h)) as nonzero h tends to zero. The open interval and finite-limit conditions ensure that this definition applies.
Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/3-1-defining-the-derivative. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
